-- Then check if there's any gap of 4+ consecutive years
WITH actor_years AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT mc.PID, TRY_CAST(m.year AS INTEGER) AS yr
    FROM M_Cast mc
    JOIN Movie m ON mc.MID = m.MID
    WHERE mc.PID IS NOT NULL
),
actor_career AS (
    SELECT PID, MIN(yr) AS first_year, MAX(yr) AS last_year,
           COUNT(DISTINCT yr) AS num_active_years
    FROM actor_years
    GROUP BY PID
),
-- Generate all years in each actor's career span
all_career_years AS (
    SELECT ac.PID, ac.first_year, ac.last_year, 
           g.value AS yr
    FROM actor_career ac
    CROSS JOIN UNNEST(range(ac.first_year, ac.last_year + 1, 1)) AS g(value)
),
-- Check if each year is active for the actor
career_with_status AS (
    SELECT acy.PID, acy.yr,
           CASE WHEN ay.yr IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_active
    FROM all_career_years acy
    LEFT JOIN actor_years ay ON acy.PID = ay.PID AND acy.yr = ay.yr
),
-- Find gaps: consecutive years where is_active = 0
-- We need to find if there's any run of 4+ consecutive zeros
-- Use a gap-finding approach with row numbers
gaps AS (
    SELECT PID, yr, is_active,
           yr - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY PID, is_active ORDER BY yr) AS grp
    FROM career_with_status
),
-- Count consecutive gap runs

    SELECT PID, is_active, grp, COUNT(*) AS run_length
    FROM gaps
    GROUP BY PID, is_active, grp
),
-- Find max gap length for each actor
max_gaps AS (
    SELECT PID, MAX(CASE WHEN is_active = 0 THEN run_length ELSE 0 END) AS max_gap
    FROM gap_runs
    GROUP BY PID
)
SELECT mg.PID, ac.first_year, ac.last_year, ac.num_active_years, mg.max_gap
FROM max_gaps mg
JOIN actor_career ac ON mg.PID = ac.PID
ORDER BY mg.max_gap DESC
